title: Note Terms — Rate Adjustments on Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
These terms describe how the contract rate of a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage moves after closing, product by product.

## The variable product

The FarmLand Variable-Rate Mortgage's rate moves on each Association Variable Base Rate history date to the new base rate plus the product's variable-rate spread less the discounts in force, never below the product's rate floor, and its installment is unchanged (the final installment absorbs the difference).

## The adjustable products

A FarmLand 3-Year, 5-Year or 10-Year Adjustable Mortgage adjusts on its next scheduled reset date:

1. the new rate is the Association Variable Base Rate in effect that day plus the product's reset margin less the discounts in force;
2. it may move by no more than the product's periodic adjustment cap up or down from the rate in force before the adjustment;
3. it may not exceed the loan's initial rate plus the product's lifetime cap over the initial rate;
4. it may not be lower than the product's rate floor;
5. it is rounded to 3 decimal places;
6. a new fixed period of the product's fixed-period months begins; and
7. the installment is re-amortised over the remaining amortization at the new rate.

## The fully fixed products

A fully fixed product — the FarmLand 15-Year Fixed Mortgage or the FarmLand 25-Year Fixed Mortgage — never adjusts.

## At a glance

| Product kind | When the rate moves | Bounds | Installment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variable | each base-rate history date | rate floor | unchanged; the final installment absorbs the difference |
| Adjustable | the next scheduled reset date | periodic cap, lifetime cap over the initial rate, rate floor | re-amortised over the remaining amortization |
| Fully fixed | never | — | unchanged |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)

A FarmLand 5-Year Adjustable Mortgage reaches its reset date. The rate in force is 6.850 percent, the loan's initial rate was 6.850 percent and an autopay discount of 0.10 is in force. Suppose the Association Variable Base Rate that day were 9.500 percent (an assumed figure).

- Base rate plus the 0.20 margin, less 0.10, is 9.600 percent.
- The periodic cap of 2.0 allows a move of no more than 2.0 points from 6.850, that is no higher than 8.850.
- The lifetime ceiling is 6.850 plus 5.0, that is 11.850; 8.850 is within it, and above the 5.25 floor.
- The new rate is 8.850 percent; a new 60-month fixed period begins and the installment is re-amortised at 8.850 percent.

Had the base rate that day been 5.000 percent instead, 5.000 plus 0.20 less 0.10 is 5.100, within 2.0 points of 6.850 but below the 5.25 floor, so the new rate would be 5.250 percent.
